This small plot behind my house is just a little piece, not even one tenth of a hectare, so I plant my cassava and cocoyam together like I always do. I do not buy fertilizer for root crops — my cassava grows well with the sweeping from the compound and the ash from my cooking fire, and the rain here is plenty so I do not need to carry water. I use the cassava stems I cut from last year's harvest, same as my mother did, and I weed it myself with my cutlass when the grass comes up. For such a small plot I do not need to call anybody to help me.
